title: Sigil and Wolf Again
premise: Silas Vasquez, a scribe bound by debt to the temple of the magicless valley, has spent her life erasing herself from every record that matters. When a feral child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Silas recognizes it from forbidden sigils in the temple archives—and learns the child is the last vessel of dragon-fire, hunted by the thing wearing King Aldric's crown. Fleeing the valley with the child and a disgraced wolf-knight who remembers too much, Silas discovers her own erased memories hold the binding ritual's missing half: she helped write it, long ago, before she chose to forget. In the burning throne room, Silas must reclaim who she was to unbind the king, sacrificing her anonymity forever but gaining a found family worth being seen by.
about_author: Hazel Brightwater is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people who hide in plain sight, drawing on years cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. She lives near a valley she insists is ordinary, with two dogs and an ever-growing collection of untranslated alphabets.

chapters.title: The Child Who Spoke First
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A mud-soaked child appears at the temple door speaking a language Silas half-remembers from sealed archive sigils. When temple wardens come asking questions, Silas hides the child and falsifies records—her first act of open rebellion. Emotional beat: fear cracking into fierce protectiveness as Silas realizes the child's words match handwriting she doesn't remember writing.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Silas and Brannoc, a wolf-knight exiled for remembering the old king. He arrives hunting the child, then kneels instead when he recognizes the dialect as pre-kingdom dragon-tongue. The three flee across the valley's border, where magic floods back into Silas like a name returning. Emotional beat: terror and wonder as Silas feels power stir memories she paid dearly to bury.

chapters.title: The Crown That Wears the Man
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. In the capital, they find King Aldric hollowed out, his crown a parasite feeding on dragon-fire—the child is its last meal. Silas deciphers her own ancient binding work and confronts the truth: she co-authored the ritual, then erased herself to escape its cost. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into resolve as Silas accepts that forgetting was never the same as innocence.

chapters.title: Last Light, First Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the throne room, Silas speaks her true name aloud—restoring her erased self—to complete the unbinding, while Brannoc holds off the crown's thralls and the child offers her fire willingly rather than by force. Aldric wakes; the crown dies guttering. Emotional beat: grief for the self she lost, joy in the family she chose, and peace as the last dragon-fire settles gently into new hands.
